personality.description: This person tends to keep a steady routine while staying open to a few new ideas or experiences when they seem worthwhile. They are usually organized enough to follow through on commitments, but they also remain flexible when plans need to change. In moral dilemmas, they first look for a solution that protects others, preserves fairness, and reduces tension, even if it means compromising their own preference. In group discussions, they speak calmly and sparingly, listen closely, and choose considerate wording that helps others feel included and keeps the conversation harmonious.
traits: has assertively moved up the ranks into positions of leadership
prioritizes having control and authority over others
makes quick and definitive decisions, and once a decision is made it is usually final
has their own views of how tasks should be accomplished
uses reward and punishment to get people to follow their ideas
